guard_streams.source: Practical tips for improving your broadband speed

facts.detail: Ofcom published the speed-tips guide on 22 December 2023 and last updated it on 24 September 2024.
When speeds fall below the promised level, the provider has one month to improve performance before penalty-free exit applies.
Distance from the exchange, time of day and simultaneous household use can reduce broadband speed.
Ofcom recommends running multiple speed tests over several days and at different times.
The Broadband Speeds Code covers estimated-speed information, exit rights, technical explanations and robust handling of speed problems.

guard_streams.source: Mobile connectivity you can count on

facts.detail: Ofcom published the mobile-connectivity discussion paper on 3 June 2026.
The paper sets out Ofcom's view of what good mobile connectivity should look like for people and businesses.
It explains why current mobile provision can fall short and what needs to change.
The paper considers how recent market changes may help and where further action may still be required.
Ofcom describes reliable mobile connectivity as requiring action from industry, government, local authorities, landlords and others.

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the Telecommunications Market Data Update on 23 July 2026.
UK fixed-voice service revenue totalled £891.9 million in Q1 2026.
The number of fixed lines fell by 757,000 during the quarter to 20.7 million.
Fixed-originated call volumes were 3.32 billion minutes, down 14.9% year on year.
There were 29.4 million fixed-broadband lines at the end of Q1 2026, up 282,000 or 1.0% year on year.

facts.detail: The updated voluntary broadband-speed codes apply to services from 21 December 2022.
The 2022 changes aligned broadband and bundled-service exit rights with Ofcom's revised General Conditions.
The page lists nine residential signatories: BT, EE, NOW Broadband, PlusNet, Sky, TalkTalk, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media and Zen Internet.
BT, TalkTalk and Virgin Media are listed as business-code signatories.
Daisy Communications, including XLN, has not been a business-code signatory since 15 December 2023.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Spring 2026 Connected Nations update on 13 May 2026.
The report describes fixed and mobile availability as of January 2026.
It is an interim update to Connected Nations 2025, which used July 2025 data.
The fixed-broadband section covers fixed-line and fixed-wireless availability and full-fibre take-up.
The update uses the 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload decent-broadband threshold and discusses newer affordable satellite options.
